    "Revenue recovery toward pre-COVID trend: FY2021 revenue of Rs 135,979 cr was depressed (~6.5% decline vs FY2020's Rs 145,452 cr) due to COVID-19 disruptions; the 5-year CAGR (FY2016-FY2021) is approximately 5.9% p.a., and we assume mean-reversion to ~9-10% growth in FY2022 (recovery year) before normalizing to ~7-8% in FY2023-24, consistent with the 5-year CAGR and L&T's strong order book of Rs 327,354 cr (8% growth y-o-y) providing revenue visibility.",
    "Net Profit (PAT) normalization: FY2021 consolidated PAT of Rs 11,583 cr included a large one-time gain from discontinued operations (Electrical & Automation divestment gain of ~Rs 8,186 cr); underlying continuing-operations PAT was only ~Rs 4,683 cr. We use the reported PAT figure of Rs 9,549 cr (FY2020) as the cleaner base and project forward at 8-10% growth, reflecting operational leverage from revenue recovery, stable PBDIT margins (~11.5%), improving RONW (16.2% in FY2021), offset by higher credit costs in Financial Services and potential cost pressures."
  ],
  "reasoning": "FY2021 is anomalous on two counts: (1) revenues declined 6.5% y-o-y due to COVID-19 lockdowns and project execution delays, significantly below the 5-year CAGR of ~5.9%; and (2) reported PAT of Rs 11,583 cr was heavily distorted by a one-time Rs 8,186 cr gain from the Electrical & Automation business divestment. Accordingly, the latest year-on-year growth rate is not a reliable projection basis, and we instead anchor to the 5-year CAGR with a recovery adjustment. The revenue forecast assumes a rebound in FY2022 (~9.6% growth) supported by a strong order book of Rs 327,354 cr, healthy domestic and international order inflows, and management's focus on infrastructure, defence, IT services and hydrocarbon segments; thereafter growth moderates to ~8% in FY2023-24. Net profit forecasts exclude the divestment windfall and are built on normalized continuing-operations profitability (~Rs 7,000-8,000 cr base adjusted for exceptional items), growing at 8-10% as margins stabilise and Financial Services credit costs normalise post-pandemic. EPS is computed on approximately 140 crore diluted shares consistent with the reported base of Rs 82.49 EPS on Rs 11,583 cr PAT implying ~140.4 cr shares."
}

Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).
